item.dc:creator: Mohammad Shahid
item.description:

The post Binance Founder CZ Could Sue Netflix Over Its FTX Series appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) is consulting lawyers over his portrayal in Netflix’s new FTX drama, The Altruists, accusing the streaming giant of defamation.

Speaking at Binance Blockchain Week in Bangkok on November 28, CZ expressed frustration over the series depicting him as a villain while presenting convicted FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) in a more sympathetic light.

He also questioned whether the series had a wider political motive.

“My guess is probably they’re trying to shape public perception to prepare for a pardon for SBF, maybe in two years, maybe in six years, maybe in ten years,” CZ said.

Bankman-Fried is currently serving a 25-year prison sentence for fraud.

The Binance founder also disputed the show’s depiction of their personal relationship.

“I’ve only met SBF like a handful of times, like maybe like five times,” he said.

CZ acknowledged that he had only watched clips of the series on social media.

The Fictional Scene That Sparked the Netflix Backlash

The controversy largely centers on a scene in episode four, where CZ pressures Bankman-Fried to give Alameda Research advance access to FTX customer orders.

This would allow Alameda to profit by trading ahead of customers, a practice known as front-running. Bankman-Fried initially refuses.

However, the show’s creator, Graham Moore, acknowledged in Vulture that the encounter was invented.

“There’s no evidence that CZ ever specifically pressured FTX to front-run,” Moore wrote.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin also questioned whether racial stereotyping influenced the portrayal.

Meanwhile, Binance co-founder Yi He challenged the show’s historical accuracy, offering her own account of FTX’s collapse.

“Narratives may matter, but so does the truth,” she wrote.

Netflix Has Faced Similar Lawsuits Before

In 2024, Scottish woman Fiona Harvey launched a $170 million lawsuit against Netflix over her alleged portrayal as a convicted stalker in Baby Reindeer. 

Netflix’s appeal was dismissed, and a jury trial is scheduled for May 18, 2027.

Netflix also settled a defamation lawsuit in 2024 over ‘When They See Us’. The company agreed to donate $1 million to the Innocence Project and move its dramatization disclaimer to the beginning of episodes.

Both cases highlight the potential legal consequences of fictionalizing real people and events.

CZ has yet to confirm whether he will formally sue Netflix.

The post Binance Founder CZ Could Sue Netflix Over Its FTX Series appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: World Liberty Financial Blames Binance for Its 50% Crash Overnight
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
World Liberty blames Binance for traders' WLFI futures losses as Justin Sun urges exchanges to delist WLFI and USD1.

The post World Liberty Financial Blames Binance for Its 50% Crash Overnight appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The WLFI token from the Trump family-backed World Liberty Financial crashed over 50% today. The altcoin lost nearly $500 million within an hour. The project is now blaming the crash on Binance. 

According to World Liberty Financial, Binance decided to force-close its futures traders’ bets overnight. Some traders reportedly lost money despite having profitable trades before Binance closed them. 

Meanwhile, Tron’s Justin Sun called on crypto exchanges to stop offering WLFI and USD1 stablecoin. Until Friday, Binance was still rewarding users with WLFI tokens for holding USD1.

World Liberty Says Binance Forcefully Liquidated Winning Traders

World Liberty pointed to a Binance system called auto-deleveraging (ADL). 

Under Binance’s rules, when traders lose more money than the exchange’s insurance fund can cover, Binance can automatically close other traders’ profitable positions to manage those losses.

This means traders can correctly predict the price movement and still have their trades forcibly closed.

A study by Gauntlet founder Tarun Chitra found that Binance relied too heavily on this system during the October 2025 market crash, more so than rival exchange Hyperliquid.

The latest closures came as WLFI’s price fell 50% in less than 11 hours on Saturday.

Binance had yet to publicly explain what happened. World Liberty directed affected traders to Binance’s customer support.

“We are aware that overnight, Binance automatically closed WLFI perpetual futures positions on both the long and short sides. WLFI had no involvement in these actions and has no control over how these positions are managed, closed, or settled,” the project wrote.

However, some traders reject that answer, calling out the Trump-backed project for shifting blame.

How Closely Are Binance and World Liberty Tied?

On Oct. 30, Binance announced a pool of 120 million WLFI tokens and up to 2.5 million USD1 for users who held USD1 on the exchange.

WLFI rewards built up until Nov. 27 and were paid out weekly. Two USD1 payouts are still scheduled, on Dec. 11 and Jan. 8. Users in the US were excluded.

On Saturday, World Liberty’s USD1 stablecoin, meant to hold $1, briefly fell to $0.94 before pulling back.

Trading firm Jump Crypto pulled 43.26 million discounted USD1 from exchanges in an hour to redeem for $1 through BitGo, Lookonchain said.

The token was already shrinking. USD1 supply stood at $2.72 billion, down about 39% from $4.47 billion on Oct. 6, Bloomberg data shows.

The post World Liberty Financial Blames Binance for Its 50% Crash Overnight appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Bitcoin’s $1 Million Bull Now Says AI Could Send It to Zero
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Chamath Palihapitiya, who once forecast $1 million Bitcoin, says AI could break it. Saylor says it can upgrade.

The post Bitcoin’s $1 Million Bull Now Says AI Could Send It to Zero appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
In 2017, famous Canadian venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya said Bitcoin would one day hit $1 million. He told his followers to invest 1% of their wealth in it. 

Now, the billionaire says Bitcoin could go to zero. His reason is AI. 

If Palihapitiya is right, the losers include every Bitcoin holder and shareholders of MicroStrategy, the Nasdaq-listed company that owns over 850,000 Bitcoin.

How a $1 Million Bull Turned on Bitcoin

Palihapitiya, a former Facebook executive, bought early at about $100 a coin, CNBC reported.  As late as August 2024, he predicted $500,000.

Then, in October, he told the Moonshots podcast that Bitcoin was capped and would one day be hacked to zero.

On Friday, his venture firm Social Capital published an essay detailing why.

“I said that crypto and Bitcoin are capped. That comment drew strong reactions, so I asked my team to review my reasoning, double-check it with experts…,” he wrote.

Why He Thinks AI Could Break Bitcoin

Bitcoin is guarded by math puzzles that would take today’s computers impossibly long to solve. That is what stops a thief from faking a signature and taking someone’s coins.

The essay argues AI could find shortcuts. It notes AI helped crack math problems this year that stood open for generations. Experts are still checking that work.

It also cites Anthropic, whose Claude model found a faster attack on a weakened version of a common cipher in July.

Anthropic says that does not affect systems in use today.

Saylor Says the Fix Is an Upgrade

Michael Saylor, whose company has spent more than $63 billion buying Bitcoin, called the essay’s core idea a fallacy.

“This thesis rests on a logical fallacy. Bitcoin isn’t software… If AI breaks encryption, all digital commerce is at risk. The solution is an upgrade to next generation encryption,” Michael Saylor challenged.

BitGo chief executive Mike Belshe also pushed back. By that logic, he said, banks and the messaging app Signal would go to zero too.

Ethereum’s foundation already ranks AI as a more urgent threat than quantum computers. Bitcoin, though, has no boss to order an upgrade. Its users must agree, and Palihapitiya calls that close to impossible.

The post Bitcoin’s $1 Million Bull Now Says AI Could Send It to Zero appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Biggest US Bank Failure Since 2024 Will Cost the FDIC $1.83 Billion
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Regulators shut United Fidelity in the biggest US bank failure since 2024. See why the FDIC expects a $1.83B loss.

The post Biggest US Bank Failure Since 2024 Will Cost the FDIC $1.83 Billion appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
US regulators closed Indiana-based United Fidelity Bank on Friday. This was America’s largest bank failure since April 2024. 

The FDIC, which insures customer deposits, must now pay nearly $1.83 billion. 

That bill equals about 31% of the bank’s assets. Depositors lose nothing. Instead, the cost falls on a fund that every insured US bank finances through quarterly fees.

Why Will This US Bank Failure Cost the FDIC So Much?

The answer sits in the loan book. 

Regulatory filings show 70.63% of United Fidelity’s loans were nonperforming on September 30. That means borrowers had stopped paying or fallen far behind.

Apartment-building loans made up 89% of United Fidelity’s lending.

The buyer priced that in. First Citizens said its winning bid carried a discount of about $2.6 billion on the assets.

It paid no premium for the deposits, and took on $4.5 billion of the $5.4 billion held.

“We believe this transaction is both financially and strategically compelling,” Chairman and CEO Frank B. Holding Jr. said in a statement, describing the deal in upbeat terms.

The loss rate also dwarfs the last failure of similar size.

Philadelphia’s Republic First Bank held about $6 billion in assets in April 2024. Its failure cost the fund $667 million, roughly 11% of assets.

Is the United Fidelity Collapse an Early Warning for Banks?

The OCC, which supervises federal savings banks, placed the lender under a consent order in 2023 over lending and risk controls.

Its problems also look concentrated. No US bank of its size reported a higher bad-loan ratio. The lender was owned by Indiana housing developer Pedcor.

Still, United Fidelity is the seventh US bank failure of 2026.

Commercial property losses already battered US regional bank stocks in early 2024.

First Citizens, which also absorbed Silicon Valley Bank’s loans in 2023, faces its first market test when its shares trade Monday. All 22 branches reopen under its name, with checks, cards, and online banking unchanged.

The post Biggest US Bank Failure Since 2024 Will Cost the FDIC $1.83 Billion appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Justin Sun Was 10 Minutes Too Late to Save FTX, Former COO Reveals
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Ex-FTX COO Constance Wang says Justin Sun offered $4 billion minutes after SBF signed FTX over to John Ray.

The post Justin Sun Was 10 Minutes Too Late to Save FTX, Former COO Reveals appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Sun offered FTX $4 billion about 10 minutes after Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) had already signed the exchange over to a bankruptcy chief, former COO Constance Wang said Saturday. The message arrived at 4:40 a.m. on November 11, 2022.

Within hours, new boss John Ray III filed for bankruptcy, which froze customers’ claims at that day’s dollar value. Sun’s offer was also a loan, and it covered only about half of FTX’s roughly $8 billion hole.

Five Days From Calm to Collapse

The account comes from Constance Wang, FTX’s former chief operating officer (COO). Within hours, new boss John Ray III put FTX into bankruptcy, and customers’ claims were frozen at that day’s dollar value.

It began on November 6, when Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) said the exchange would sell its FTT, the token FTX issued. About $6 billion left FTX in 72 hours, Wang revealed in a post.

At 3 a.m. on November 8, SBF called her to a war room. Someone showed her the balance sheet. The bottom line was a big negative number.

Binance agreed to buy FTX that day. Then it walked away, shortly after receiving FTX’s books. Wang still questions why.

“I wondered whether CZ had ever wanted more than a look at the books, though I had no way of knowing,” Wang said Saturday.

Would $4 Billion Have Saved FTX?

SBF has said yes for years. In December 2022 draft testimony to Congress, he described an unnamed offer “for billions of dollars” that came minutes too late, according to the ABA Journal. He blamed his lawyers for rushing the filing.

Wang’s post now names Sun and the figure.

The figures point the other way. Sun’s money was a loan backed by FTX’s own investments, not fresh cash. It covered about half of the roughly $8 billion hole SBF described to investors.

The courts sided with the numbers. In June 2026, a US appeals court rejected SBF’s claim that FTX would eventually have had enough to repay customers. His appeal mandate later locked in a 25-year sentence.

Wang’s story lands as Netflix’s The Altruists series and an Amazon FTX documentary retell the collapse.

For creditors, the clock never restarted. The estate is repaying them in dollars at 2022 values, not in the crypto they held.

The post Justin Sun Was 10 Minutes Too Late to Save FTX, Former COO Reveals appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Binance Picks Bhutan’s Unfinished City Over Singapore and Hong Kong
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Binance won in-principle approval in Bhutan from a 26-day-old central bank. Here is what it allows, and what it does not.

The post Binance Picks Bhutan’s Unfinished City Over Singapore and Hong Kong appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange is planning an Asian hub in a Himalayan city that is still being built.

Gelephu, a town on Bhutan’s southern border with India, announced its own central bank on November 2. Less than a month later, Binance received an in-principle approval from that bank.

The hub sits outside Singapore and Hong Kong, Asia’s established crypto centers. It cannot yet serve a single user, and the supervisor that would oversee those users is weeks old.

Why Bhutan Instead of Singapore or Hong Kong?

Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) is a 4,046-square-kilometre special administrative region announced in 2023 by Bhutan’s king.

The exchange plans to establish local operations and hire Bhutanese employees. A full operating licence remains pending.

Spanning more than five times the size of Singapore, the city is being designed around renewable energy, financial innovation and advanced technology. 

However, it is a largely unfinished development.

So far, its first renovated commercial building houses administrative offices, while 108 Buddhist monuments were erected earlier this month.

Around 40 buildings are awaiting redevelopment. Its international airport is scheduled to open in 2029.

On November 2, Bhutan announced transforming the city’s existing financial regulator into an autonomous central bank.

A Unique Regulatory Backdoor?

Binance’s Singapore subsidiary withdrew its licence application in 2021. The country further tightened its regulations on overseas-facing crypto businesses in June 2025. 

Meanwhile, Binance remains absent from Hong Kong’s licensed crypto exchange register.

Bhutan offers an alternative through its dedicated financial regulatory framework.

Bhutan Is Already Attracting Major Crypto Firms

Gelephu’s official regulatory register currently lists 14 licensed financial entities, including several digital asset businesses.

Matrixport, BTSE, Ceffu, KairosX, 8020 Finance and RedotX have already secured licences. Binance’s proposed entry could further strengthen this emerging crypto ecosystem.

What It Means for Binance’s Asian Users

Binance plans to expand into five Asian markets in 2027, according to Reuters.

A regulated regional base could support wider product availability and improve regional compliance. 

However, a Bhutanese licence would not automatically grant Binance permission to serve customers in Singapore, Hong Kong or other restricted markets.

For Bhutan, the opportunity is considerable. A country historically known for its Buddhist monasteries is now competing for a share of Asia’s lucrative digital asset economy.

The post Binance Picks Bhutan’s Unfinished City Over Singapore and Hong Kong appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: XRP Holders Want to Burn 31 Billion Tokens, But Ripple CTO Pushes Back
item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz says XRP Ledger validators cannot force Ripple to burn its escrowed XRP. He added that even more than 80% support would not change that. His comments respond to a growing campaign by holders. However, the debate also reveals how XRP Ledger governance works. What Is the XRP Escrow Burn Campaign?

The post XRP Holders Want to Burn 31 Billion Tokens, But Ripple CTO Pushes Back appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz says XRP Ledger validators cannot force Ripple to burn its escrowed XRP. He added that even more than 80% support would not change that.

His comments respond to a growing campaign by holders. However, the debate also reveals how XRP Ledger governance works.

What Is the XRP Escrow Burn Campaign?

The XRP escrow is a set of time-locked accounts that hold Ripple’s XRP and release it gradually. A token burn permanently removes coins from circulation.

On November 16, a group called Make XRP Great Again sent an open letter to Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse. The group demanded that Ripple burn 31.1 billion escrowed XRP by March 31, 2027.

The campaign quickly gained traction among XRP holders on social media.

Ripple reported about 31.1 billion XRP at the time of writing.

Meanwhile, Ripple plans to release 1 billion XRP from escrow on December 1.

Supporters argue that a burn would reduce supply.

In theory, lower supply could ease selling pressure on XRP over time. Critics have long argued that Ripple’s large holdings weigh on the XRP price.

Can XRP Validators Force Ripple to Burn Tokens?

According to Schwartz, the answer is no. As one of the XRP Ledger’s original architects, he explained on X that the ledger has no coercive mechanism at all.

An amendment needs 29 of 35 validator votes, or more than 80%.

It must also keep that support for two weeks before activating.

Still, Schwartz said a majority cannot force dissenters to accept its rules. Validators pushing a burn amendment would simply isolate themselves from the network.

In other words, a supermajority can change its own rules but cannot seize Ripple’s escrow. Schwartz added that the same logic applies to a minority.

Back in February 2024, he noted that Ripple itself could mimic a burn. It could send escrow releases to a black-holed account that no one controls.

Meanwhile, XRP trades near $0.95, down nearly 30% in a month. For now, the escrow remains firmly in Ripple’s hands.

The post XRP Holders Want to Burn 31 Billion Tokens, But Ripple CTO Pushes Back appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Trump-Backed WLFI Falls 50% as World Liberty Dumps Ethereum at a $19M Loss
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
WLFI crashes 50% after World Liberty Financial sells $20 million in Ethereum at a $19 million loss. Here's what moved.

The post Trump-Backed WLFI Falls 50% as World Liberty Dumps Ethereum at a $19M Loss appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
WLFI, the token of the Trump family-backed crypto venture World Liberty Financial, fell about 50% in under 11 hours on Saturday, Binance data shows. The crash came after the venture’s reserve wallet sold about $20 million in Ethereum (ETH) at a steep loss.

The ETH cost about $3,244 per coin last year and went for roughly $1,655. That locked in a loss of about $19.26 million. Most of the token’s slide came later, between 03:00 and 05:00 UTC, when WLFI lost more than 40% of its value.

How World Liberty Financial Sold Its Ethereum

Blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that the wallet sold 10,600 ETH worth $17.58 million. It also sold 1,378 mETH worth $2.48 million.

mETH is a token from the Mantle network that stands in for staked ETH.

The trades ran through CoW Protocol, a platform that settles orders in batches, Arkham Intelligence data shows. The proceeds landed as 17.58 million USDC and 2.48 million USD1.

USD1 is the dollar-pegged stablecoin that World Liberty Financial issues itself.

The wallet then sent 2.5 million USD1 to Dolomite, a crypto lending platform. About two hours later, 2,000 ETH worth $3.31 million moved back to the reserve from Dolomite.

Will World Liberty Sell More of Its Reserve?

Crypto trader AuroraQAQ, who tracked the sale on X (Twitter), took issue with the wallet’s label.

“A ‘strategic reserve’ selling at half its cost basis is capitulation, not strategy — and it was executed on-chain via CoW Swap, not announced,” they noted.

The sale comes three weeks after BeInCrypto reported that a WLFI buyback plan could draw on USD1 reserve income. Part of the ETH proceeds has now been parked in that same stablecoin.

Traders are now watching two things. One is whether the reserve wallet sells more ETH. The other is whether ETH holds near $1,650, the level the reserve sold into.

Justin Sun Calls for WLFI and USD1 Delistings

Tron founder Justin Sun responded to the crash on X, accusing World Liberty insiders of fraud and calling on exchanges and regulators to act.

“Today’s WLFI episode is just another rerun of insider circular lending to cash out, unauthorized insider selling, the illegal freezing of investor assets, and investor fraud. I call on major exchanges, regulators, judicial authorities, and the courts to take prompt action against WLFI and USD1…,” Sun wrote.

The fight may also be personal for Sun. He is suing World Liberty in a $45 million fraud case after the firm froze his WLFI tokens, a dispute now in a fight over sanctions. World Liberty has called the freeze a routine security step.

Sun wants warning lists, immediate delistings, deposit restrictions, and disclosure of where the funds went. He also alleged that team members have been mass-deleting social media posts and communications. These claims are Sun’s allegations and have not been tested in court.

The post Trump-Backed WLFI Falls 50% as World Liberty Dumps Ethereum at a $19M Loss appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: OKX CEO Dismisses $2 Billion Hack Rumors After Friday Night Crypto Panic
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
OKX CEO Star Xu dismissed a viral $2 billion hack rumor as fake news. See what the claim and public wallet data show.

The post OKX CEO Dismisses $2 Billion Hack Rumors After Friday Night Crypto Panic appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
OKX CEO Star Xu has dismissed a viral claim that hackers had stolen more than $2 billion from the crypto exchange, calling it “fake news.”

The fears came barely a month after Binance lost about $6.3 billion to hackers, the largest crypto theft on record. That theft was real, and Binance halted all customer withdrawals while it investigated.

Where Did the OKX Hack Rumor Come From?

The claim surfaced on Friday, when reports suggested OKX had “just been hacked for over 2 billion dollars.” It named no wallets, shared no transaction records, and cited no source.

Even so, the claims went viral, hugely because of scares surrounding the recent Binance hack and a wider incident reports in the US.

OKX CEO has however denied the report, pointing to public blockchain records as proof.

“Fake news. One of the fundamental strengths of crypto is on-chain transparency. On-chain transactions are publicly verifiable. Facts speak louder than rumors,” Xu articulated.

He added that OKX would use the episode as motivation to keep improving its security.

What Do OKX’s Public Wallets Show?

Exchanges keep customer deposits in digital wallets whose balances anyone can view on public blockchains. Data tracker DefiLlama counted about $26 billion in known OKX wallets on Saturday. A $2 billion theft would equal roughly 7% of that.

Rumors have cost OKX before. In June 2024, complaints of stolen user funds drove over $633 million in outflows from the exchange in seven days, BeInCrypto reported at the time.

The stakes now reach Wall Street. In March, NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange took a board seat at OKX at a $25 billion valuation. The two firms opened OKX-ICE tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23.

The post OKX CEO Dismisses $2 Billion Hack Rumors After Friday Night Crypto Panic appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: S&P 500 Achieves Its Best Thanksgiving Rally Since 2008. What’s Next?
item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
The S&P 500 surged 5.6% this week, its best Thanksgiving week since the 2008 financial crisis. It also marked the index’s biggest weekly gain since April 2025. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq rallied even harder. Still, the backdrop differs sharply from 2008, and key data now looms. Nasdaq and S&P 500 Enjoy Thanksgiving Rally The Nasdaq climbed

The post S&P 500 Achieves Its Best Thanksgiving Rally Since 2008. What’s Next? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The S&P 500 surged 5.6% this week, its best Thanksgiving week since the 2008 financial crisis. It also marked the index’s biggest weekly gain since April 2025.

Meanwhile, the Nasdaq rallied even harder. Still, the backdrop differs sharply from 2008, and key data now looms.

Nasdaq and S&P 500 Enjoy Thanksgiving Rally

The Nasdaq climbed 6.7% over the same stretch. Just one week earlier, the index had erased all of its 2026 gains amid heavy tech and AI selling. That swing marked one of the sharpest turnarounds of the year so far.

This rapid reversal caught many traders off guard. In fact, the Nasdaq 100 posted its largest swings since April 2025 during the week.

Earlier in the period, AI and semiconductor stocks had tumbled after several volatile sessions. Then, buyers returned aggressively and fueled a strong relief rally.

The comparison with 2008 stands out.

Back then, the only larger Thanksgiving-week gain since 1950 came after a nearly 50% crash. Moreover, stocks fell almost 25% more before bottoming in March 2009.

This time, the setup looks far healthier. The S&P 500 had slipped only about 12% from its October record before buyers stepped in. That smaller pullback points to a correction, not a crisis.

Will the Stock Market Rebound In December?

Friday’s shortened Black Friday session extended the gains. The S&P 500 rose about 1.6% and hit one-week highs near 7,325. It then settled around 7,297.

Trading volumes stayed light because of the holiday. Even so, the upward momentum held.

Next week, investors will focus on several key reports:

  • Non-farm payrolls and unemployment data.
  • The ISM services PMI.
  • University of Michigan consumer sentiment.

Together, these reports could show whether the economy remains strong enough to support higher stock prices.

The rebound also spread to other assets. Gold climbed above $3,600, while silver topped $43 as the tech sell-off eased.

Bitcoin trades near $59,700 and looked poised to end a seven-week losing streak. However, it continued to lag the equity rebound, as crypto sentiment stayed in extreme fear.

Analysts also warned about weekend positioning ahead of the Fed’s blackout period. Ultimately, interest rate expectations will likely shape the next move for both stocks and crypto.

The post S&P 500 Achieves Its Best Thanksgiving Rally Since 2008. What’s Next? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: America Blacklisted VTB Over Iran. Now Russia's No. 2 Bank Sells Bitcoin
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
VTB, a Russian bank the US blacklisted over Iran, now sells Bitcoin. See who can buy and which coins the US can freeze.

The post America Blacklisted VTB Over Iran. Now Russia's No. 2 Bank Sells Bitcoin appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Clients of VTB can now buy Bitcoin (BTC) in the bank’s investment app. Russia’s second-largest lender switched on crypto trading on November 27, ten weeks after the US Treasury named it one of the world’s most heavily sanctioned financial institutions.

Washington blacklisted VTB in September for helping Iran evade sanctions and told foreign banks to cut ties. VTB says buying, holding and recording the coins all happens on Russian infrastructure.

Washington Can Freeze Some Coins Russians Buy, but Not Bitcoin

Russia’s approved list for ordinary buyers includes Bitcoin, Ethereum (ETH) and Tether’s USDT, a token pegged to the US dollar. Tether can freeze USDT at specific addresses. Bitcoin has no issuer with that power.

By July 2026, Tether had blocked 9,597 addresses holding $5.69 billion in USDT, according to security firm BlockSec.

In March 2025, Tether helped the US Secret Service freeze $23 million tied to the sanctioned Russian exchange Garantex, Tether said.

Garantex then used A7A5, a ruble-pegged token, to give customers hit by that crackdown access to their accounts again. The Treasury sanctioned its Kyrgyz issuer, Old Vector, in August 2025.

In April 2026, Tether froze $344 million in USDT after a tip from the Treasury’s sanctions office. Those addresses were tied to Iran’s central bank the next day.

The Bank of Russia has flagged the same risk. At a Crypto Summit 2026 panel moderated by BeInCrypto CIS editor-in-chief Vladimir Arkhiereysky, the regulator’s Kirill Pronin said he was not sure most investors understand that

“…centralized, centrally issued tokens on the corresponding protocols in open blockchains are fully controlled and are subject to blocking, burning, monitoring, and so on.”

Kirill Pronin, Bank of Russia

Who Can Trade at VTB, and How Much

Only qualified investors, a Russian status for experienced or wealthier clients, can trade at VTB for now. They deal directly with the bank rather than on an exchange.

Every buyer must first pass a Bank of Russia test, answering at least seven of eight questions correctly, RBC reported. Buyers without qualified status face a yearly cap of 300,000 rubles per broker.

Exchange crypto trading in Russia starts in December. The country’s biggest stock exchange is under US sanctions too.

The Treasury’s September order told foreign institutions dealing with VTB they “should cut off those relationships immediately.”

The post America Blacklisted VTB Over Iran. Now Russia's No. 2 Bank Sells Bitcoin appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Bitcoin Treasury Titans Clash Over Whether BTC Is Money or Just Savings
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Saylor and Strive's Matt Cole push back on Jeffrey Tucker's claim that Bitcoin fails as money. Here's what's at stake.

The post Bitcoin Treasury Titans Clash Over Whether BTC Is Money or Just Savings appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Most Americans get paid in dollars and park their savings in stocks, gold, or a home. On Friday, MicroStrategy chairman Michael Saylor said Bitcoin (BTC) is competing for the savings, not the paycheck.

Saylor and Strive CEO Matt Cole were answering economist Jeffrey Tucker, who argued that an asset nobody trades with cannot be money. Their two companies hold about 894,700 BTC combined, exposure their shareholders carry through the stock.

What Did Jeffrey Tucker Say About Bitcoin?

Tucker founded the Brownstone Institute, a US think tank. On Friday, he said Bitcoin backers had tried to imagine a store of value into existence and make it the world’s most valuable asset.

He added that nothing in monetary history supports that idea.

The criticism comes from a former insider. Tucker was an early Bitcoin promoter, but he has said he soured on the network after the blocksize wars, a 2015 to 2017 fight over how many transactions Bitcoin should handle, according to a Brownstone episode description.

How Did Saylor and Strive’s Matt Cole Respond?

In his pushback, Cole aimed at defenders of the US dollar. He blamed deficit spending funded by money printing.

“There is no such thing as money you can debase without consequence. You did this to yourself. You believed that you could spend money you didn’t have, print the difference, and keep the dollar as the world’s reserve currency forever,” the Strive executive challenged.

Cole built his post out of Tucker’s own lines. He swapped “Give it up Bitcoiners” for “Give it up dollar maxis” and kept Tucker’s closing claim that nothing in the history of money backs the other side’s “fantasy.”

The borrowing behind his jab is large. Total US public debt passed $40 trillion for the first time in August, according to Treasury data.

However, the dollar still holds its reserve status. It made up 56.7% of central bank foreign exchange reserves in the second quarter of 2026, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

Saylor also responded to Tucker, separating the act of paying from the act of saving.

“Jeffrey, a gold-backed banknote could pay the baker, the miller, and the farmer while the gold stayed in the vault. Today people pay in dollars and save in gold, stocks, and real estate. Bitcoin is competing for those savings.”

Saylor was describing how the gold standard worked. Paper notes changed hands in daily trade, while the gold backing them stayed in reserve.

That link broke for the US dollar in 1971, when President Richard Nixon ended the conversion of dollars into gold. Since then, the dollar has had no fixed tie to any physical asset.

Both executives have put company money behind the savings view. Strive kept adding Bitcoin as prices fell in November, while MicroStrategy slowed its Bitcoin buying, BeInCrypto reported.

Why Does the Money Debate Matter for MicroStrategy and Strive Investors?

MicroStrategy holds 851,305 BTC and Strive holds 43,404, ranking first and fourth among public companies running Bitcoin treasuries.

MicroStrategy had paid an average of $75,456 per coin as of early November, per its filing. However, Bitcoin has since slipped below that level, leaving Strategy’s stack underwater. MSTR shares have also lost nearly half their value over the past year.

Meanwhile, 196 public companies now hold about 1.24 million BTC, the same tracker shows. That model rests on holding coins, not spending them, which is the side of the argument Saylor and Cole defended on Friday.
